title: How Google Really Makes Money (You're Not the Customer)
description:
Alphabet brought in $402.8 billion in 2025, yet you never pay to search. In this file we open the money machine behind Google: two Stanford students and a garage in Menlo Park, BackRub, the AdWords auction, the 2004 IPO, Android and YouTube, where the money comes from today, the billions Google pays to be the default search engine, the antitrust ruling, and the AI bet that turned Google Cloud into a rocket, with the latest numbers.

{CHAPTERS}

Sources: Alphabet Q3 2026 results (Form 8-K, October 2026); Alphabet Q4 and full year 2025 results; Google (Our Story); Yahoo News (On this day: the garage where Google was founded); CNN Money (Google IPO, 2004); Bloomberg / AppleInsider (Google's payments to Apple, 2022); NPR (Google antitrust remedies ruling, September 2025); Outlook Business (Alphabet 2026 capex and cloud backlog); 9to5Google; eWeek (Google buys YouTube); Android Authority (Google buys Android).

All figures are rounded. Forecasts are company guidance. This video is for education only, not investment advice.
